translations.text: The words of Amos, who was in Akkarim of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. And he says:
The Lord spoke from Zion and gave his voice from Jerusalem. The pastures of the flocks mourned, and the heights of Carmel dried up.
And the Lord says: “For three acts of lawlessness by Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they cut apart the pregnant women of Gilead with iron saws.”
I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will consume the foundations of the son of Hadad.

I will shatter the bars of Damascus and destroy the inhabitants of the plains of On. I will slaughter the people from among the men of Haran, and the chosen people of the Syrians will be taken captive, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: For three acts of wickedness by Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they took Solomon's captives captive to confine them in Edom.
I will send fire upon the walls of Gaza, and it will consume its foundations.
I will destroy the inhabitants of Ashdod, and the people will be removed from Ashkelon. I will bring my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says the Lord God.

Thus says the Lord: For three acts of wickedness by Tyre, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they confined Solomon's captives in Edom and did not remember the covenant between brothers.
I will send fire upon the walls of Tyre, and it will consume its foundations.

Thus says the Lord: For three acts of wickedness by Edom, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because he pursued his brother with the sword and destroyed his brother on the earth. He seized his terror as a testimony and preserved his insolence in hostility.
I will send fire into Teman, and fire will consume the foundations of its walls.

Thus says the Lord: For three acts of wickedness by the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead to enlarge their borders.
I will kindle fire upon the walls of Rabbah, and it will consume its foundations amid shouting on the day of battle. It will be shaken on the day of its end.
Their kings, their priests, and their princes will go into captivity together, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: For three acts of wickedness by Moab, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they burned the bones of the kings of Edom to ashes.
I will send fire upon Moab, and fire will consume the foundations of its cities. Moab will die in weakness, amid shouting and the sound of a trumpet.
I will destroy the judge from its midst and slaughter all its princes along with him, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: For three acts of wickedness by the children of Judah, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they rejected the law of the Lord and did not keep his commands. They led them astray with their worthless idols, which they made and which their fathers followed.
I will send fire upon Judah, and it will consume the foundations of Jerusalem.
Thus says the Lord: For three acts of wickedness by Israel, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they sold the righteous person for silver and the needy person for shoes.
They trample the dust of the earth and beat the heads of the poor, and they twist the paths of the humble. A father and a son go in to the same prostitute, profaning the name of their God.
They spread their garments as a curtain beneath themselves and beneath the altar, and they drink wine obtained through false accusations in the house of their god.
But I removed the Amorite from before them, whose height was the height of a cedar and who was strong as an oak. I removed his fruit above and his roots below.
And I brought you up from the land of the Egyptians and led you around in the wilderness for forty years, so that you might inherit the land of the Amorites.
“And I took some of your sons to be prophets and some of your young men to be Nazirites. Is this not so, children of Israel?” says the Lord.
But you gave my Nazirites wine to drink and commanded the prophets not to prophesy.
“Therefore, behold, I will roll beneath you, just as a wagon full of sheaves rolls.”
Escape will fail the swift runner; the strong will not prevail by their strength, and the warrior will not save his own life.
“The archer shall not be able to stand his ground, the swift-footed shall not escape, and the horseman shall not save his own life.”
His heart will have no strength; naked, he will be pursued on that day, says the Lord.
Hear this message that the Lord has spoken against you, house of Israel, against all the peoples whom I brought up from the land of the Egyptians.
But I chose you from all the nations of the earth. Therefore I will exact punishment from you for all your evil deeds.
Will two ever walk together unless they know one another?
Will a lion roar from the forest unless it has caught prey? Will a lion cub raise its voice from its thicket unless it has seized something?
Will a bird fall to the ground without a hunter? Will a trap spring on the ground without catching anything?
Can a trumpet be sounded in a city without the people being alarmed? Can disaster occur in a city without the Lord having brought it about?
Therefore the Lord God will do nothing unless he reveals his plan to his servants the prophets.
A lion roars, and who will not tremble? The Lord God has spoken, and who will not prophesy?

Proclaim it in the provinces of the Assyrians and in the provinces of the land of the Egyptians, and say: Gather on the mountain of Samaria and see the many astonishing things within it and the violence within it.
It did not recognize the calamity that was to come upon it, says the Lord—they who stored up lawlessness and misery in their provinces.
Therefore this is what the Lord God says to Tyre: The land surrounding you will be laid waste, all your strength will be broken, and your provinces will be plundered.

For this is what the Lord says: Just as a shepherd might rescue two legs or a piece of an ear from a lion’s mouth, so will the children of Israel who live in Samaria escape, opposite the nation and among the people of Damascus.
Priests, hear and bear witness to the house of Jacob, says the Lord Almighty.
For on that day, when I exact punishment from Israel for its ungodliness, I will also punish the altar of Bethel. The horns of the altar will be shattered and fall to the ground.
I will demolish the winged palaces along with the summer palaces. The ivory palaces will be destroyed, and many other palaces will fall, says the Lord.
Hear the word of the Lord, cows of Bashan who are on the mountains of Samaria, who oppress the poor and trample the needy, who said to your masters: Bring us wine so that we may drink.
The Lord swears by his holiness: Behold, days will come upon you when they will take you away with weapons and throw those who are with you into heated cauldrons.
You will go out naked, facing one another, and you will fall on Mount Remman, says the Lord.
Enter Bethel and act wickedly; in Gilgal multiply your wickedness. Bring your sacrifices in the morning and your tithes on the third day.
They read the laws outside and called for thanksgivings. Proclaim that this is what the children of Israel loved, says the Lord.
“And I inflicted [?] toothache in all your cities and a lack of bread in all your places, yet you did not return to me,” says the Lord.

I also withheld rain from you three months before the harvest. I sent rain on one city and did not send rain on another city. I will water one plot, while another, on which I send no rain, will dry up.
Two or three cities will gather in one city to drink water, but they will not have enough. Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

“I struck you with scorching heat and inflicted [?] blight. You multiplied your gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees, but the caterpillar ate them. Even so, you did not return to me,” says the Lord.

I sent death upon you on the road of the Egyptians, and I killed your young men with the sword, along with the capture of your horses. I consumed your camps with the fire of my wrath. Yet even so you did not return to me, says the Lord.
I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a burning stick rescued from the fire. Yet even so you did not return to me, says the Lord.
Therefore I will do this to you, Israel. And because I am going to do this to you, prepare to call upon the name of the Lord your God, Israel.

For behold, I am the one who establishes the heavens and establishes the winds, who proclaims his anointed one among human beings, who makes the dawn and the mist, and who ascends the heights of the earth. The Lord God Almighty is his name.
Hear these words, this lament that I take up over you.
The house of Israel has fallen, and the virgin of Israel will never rise again. She has been cast down upon her own land, and there is no one to raise her up.
For thus says the Lord God: In the city from which a thousand went out, a hundred will remain; and in the one from which a hundred went out, ten will remain for the house of Israel.
For thus says the Lord to the house of Israel: Seek me and you will live.
“Do not seek Bethel, do not enter Gilgal, and do not go up to the Well of the Oath, for Gilgal shall surely be taken captive, and Bethel shall become as though it had never existed.”
Seek the Lord and you will live, lest the house of Joseph blaze like fire and the fire consume it, with no one to extinguish it for the house of Israel.
He makes justice in the heights and has established righteousness upon the earth.

He makes and renews all things, turns the shadow of death into dawn, and darkens day into night. He calls for the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth. The Lord Almighty is his name.
He brings destruction upon the mighty and brings misery upon fortresses.
They hated those who rebuked them at the gates, and they treated holy words as unclean.
Therefore, because you beat the poor and took choice bribes from them, you will build splendid houses but will not live in them; you will plant desirable vineyards but will not drink their wine.
For I know your many acts of ungodliness, and your sins are grievous. You trampled the righteous underfoot, accepting payments, and turned the poor aside at the gates.
Therefore the wise person will remain silent at that time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live, and the Lord God Almighty will be with you, as you have said.
If you hate evil and love good, establish justice at your gates, so that the Lord God may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore thus says the Lord God Almighty: There will be lamentation in every square, and on every road they will say, “Alas! Alas!” The farmer will be called to mourning and lamentation and to the wailers.
And there will be lamentation on every road, for I will pass through your midst, says the Lord.
Woe to anyone who longs for the day of the Lord! What have you to do with the day of the Lord? It is darkness and not light.
It is as if a man fled from a lion and a bear met him, or he fled into a house, leaned his hand against the wall, and a snake bit him.
Is not the day of the Lord darkness and not light, gloom without any brightness in it?
“I hate and reject your festivals, and I will not savor your annual celebrations.”
For even if you offer your burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not accept them, and I will not look upon your splendid peace offerings.
Take the sound of your songs away from me; I will not listen to the music of your flutes.
Let justice surge like water, and righteousness like a boundless torrent.
Did you offer me slaughtered animals and sacrifices in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
You carried the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Remphan, their images that you made for yourselves.
I will deport you beyond Damascus, says the Lord God, whose name is Almighty.
Woe to those who despise Zion and trust in the mountain of Samaria! They stripped the nations of their power, and the house of Israel entered among them.
Go, all of you, to Calneh and see; go from there to great Hamath Rabbah, and go down to Gath of the Philistines, stronger than all those cities. Are their territories greater than your territories?
You who are coming to the day of calamity, who are drawing near to reach false sabbaths,
who sleep on ivory couches and luxuriate on your beds, and eat young goats from the flocks and suckling calves from the herds,
who danced to the sound of flutes, which you considered lasting and not passing away,
and drink clarified wine and anoint yourselves with fragrant oil, yet feel no pain over Joseph’s ruin.
Therefore they will now be led into captivity from the rule of tyrants, and the neighing of Ephraim’s horses will cease.
For the Lord has sworn by himself, says the Lord God of hosts: I will make all Jacob’s pride loathsome, and I will hate his lands and remove his cities with all their inhabitants.
And if ten men remain in one house, they will die.
The survivors will take their family members and go down to carry their bones out of the house. They will say to those standing in front of the house, “Is anyone else left there with you?”
He will say, “No.” And let him not say, “Be silent,” for this is because they did not name the name of the Lord.
For behold, the Lord will give a command and strike the great mansions with destruction and the small mansions with splitting.
Will horses gallop over rocks, or be still among mares? For you have turned justice into wrath and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness.
You rejoiced in things of no substance, saying, “Have we not acquired horns by our own strength?”
Therefore, behold, I will raise up against you, house of Israel, says the Lord God of hosts, a nation that will oppress you, so that you can no longer enter Hamath or reach the western ravine.
This is what the Lord God showed me: behold, a brood of locusts was coming in the morning, and behold, a young mule, King Gog.
When it finishes eating the vegetation of the land, I say, “Lord God, spare them! For who will raise Jacob up? He is so small.”
The Lord relented concerning this. “This, too, shall not happen,” says the Lord.
This is what the Lord God showed me: behold, the Lord God called for judgment by fire, and it consumed the great depths and consumed the allotted land.
I say, “Lord God, stop this! For who will raise Jacob up? He is so small.”
The Lord relented concerning this. “This, too, shall not happen,” says the Lord God.
This is what the Lord God showed me: behold, a man stood upon a wall of adamant, with a piece of adamant in his hand.
The Lord says to me, “What do you see, Amos?” I say, “A diamond.” The Lord says to me, “Behold, I will set a diamond among my people Israel, and I will no longer pass them by.”
The altars of laughter will be destroyed, and the temples of Israel will be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent word to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying, “Amos is gathering crowds against you within the house of Israel, and the land cannot endure all his words.”
For this is what Amos says: “Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be taken captive from its land.”
Amaziah said to Amos, “Seer, leave and go to the land of Judea. Live there and prophesy there.
But do not prophesy in Bethel anymore, for it is the king’s sanctuary and the royal house.”
Amos answered Amaziah, “I was not a prophet or a prophet’s son, but I was a shepherd and gathered mulberries.
The Lord took me from the flocks, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go and prophesy against my people Israel.’
Now hear the word of the Lord. You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not gather crowds against the house of Jacob.’

Therefore, this is what the Lord says: ‘Your wife will become a prostitute in your city, your sons and daughters will fall by the sword, your land will be divided by a measuring line, and you will die in an unclean land. Israel will certainly be taken captive from its own land.’”
This is what the Lord God showed me: there was a birdcatcher’s implement.
He said, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “A birdcatcher’s implement.” The Lord said to me, “The end has come upon my people Israel, and I will no longer pass them by.”
“The roofs of the temple will lament on that day,” says the Lord. “Many will fall, and I will impose silence everywhere.”
Hear this, you who oppressed the needy in the morning and deprived the poor in the evening,
and said, “When will the new moon be over, so that we can make a profit, and the Sabbath, so that we can open the storehouses, make the measure small, enlarge the weight, and use false scales,
buy the poor for silver and the needy for the price of sandals, and make a profit in all our trading?”
The Lord swears by the pride of Jacob: “None of your deeds shall ever be forgotten.”
Because of this the earth will be shaken, and all its inhabitants will mourn. Its destruction will rise like a river and subside like the river of Egypt.
“On that day,” says the Lord God, “the sun will set at noon, and the light on the earth will grow dark in the daytime.

I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into laments. I will put sackcloth on every body and baldness on every head. I will make it like mourning for a loved one, and for those who are with him it will be like a day of pain.
Look, days are coming,” says the Lord God, “when I will send a famine upon the land—not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord.
The waters will be troubled from sea to sea, and from north to east they will run to seek the word of the Lord, but they will not find it.
On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will suffer from thirst,
those who swear by the atonements of Samaria and say, ‘Your god lives, Dan,’ and ‘Your god lives, Beersheba.’ They will fall and never rise again.”

I saw the Lord standing over the altar, and he said, “Strike the altar, and the doorposts will shake. Cut them down onto everyone’s heads, and I will kill the rest of them with the sword. No fugitive among them will survive, and none who escape will get away.
For even if they hide in the underworld, my hand will drag them out from there; and even if they climb into heaven, I will bring them down from there.

Even if they hide on the heights of Carmel, I will search them out and take them from there. Even if they disappear from my sight into the depths of the sea, I will command the serpent there to bite them.
Even if they go into captivity before their enemies, I will command the sword there, and it will destroy them. I will set my eyes upon them for harm and not for good.”
And the Lord God Almighty, who approaches the earth and shakes it—all its inhabitants shall mourn, and its end shall rise like a river and sink like the river of Egypt.
He who builds his ascent in heaven and establishes his promise on earth, who calls the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth—the Lord Almighty is his name.
“Are you not like the Ethiopians to me, children of Israel?” says the Lord. “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of the Egyptians, the Philistines from Cappadocia, and the Syrians from Bothora?”
“Look, the eyes of the Lord are upon that kingdom of sinners, and I will remove it from the face of the earth. Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” says the Lord.
“For look, I will give the command and scatter you, house of Israel, among all the nations, as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not a particle of it will fall to the ground.
“All the sinners of my people will die by the sword, those who said, ‘Disasters will neither approach us nor overtake us.’
“On that day I will raise up David’s fallen tent. I will restore its collapsed parts and raise up its demolished parts again, and I will rebuild it as in the days of old,
“so that the rest of humanity may seek me, along with all the nations over whom my name has been called,” says the Lord, who does these things.

“Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when the threshing will overtake the grape harvest, and grapes will ripen at sowing time. The mountains will pour forth sweetness, and all the hills will be thickly wooded.
“I will bring back the captives of my people Israel. They will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them; they will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
“I will plant them in their own land, and they will never again be driven from their land, which I have given them,” says the Lord God Almighty.
